description.narrative:
The general purpose of the second phase of the inclusive market project will be to enhance the i) to intensification of agroecological agriculture, ii) conscious use and consumption of resources and products and iii) social inclusion of the vulnerable population, of agri-food systems.
This will be done through 6 specific objectives:
- To facilitate access to international and national markets for agri-food products, promoting conscious food consumption.
- To facilitate the access of family productive units to adequate and innovative services, inputs, technology, and capacities for the intensification of agroecological agriculture and the efficient and sustainable use of resources.
- To promote the financial inclusion of men and women through i) access to microcredits and other forms of financing, ii) microinsurance for risk transfer and iii) financial education.
- To strengthen the capability of public and private institutions to support the economic, social, and environmental resilience of the target group
- To strengthen access to resources, services, and opportunities to expand capacities and skills that contribute to the empowerment of women and inclusion
- To enhance access to information, knowledge and systematized experiences on mechanisms, approaches, tools, methodologies, and others that contribute to advocacy on the issues prioritized by the project.

Det allmänna syftet med den andra fasen av det inkluderande marknadsprojektet är att påverka: i) intensifieringen av agroekologiskt jordbruk, ii) medveten användning och konsumtion av resurser och produkter och iii) social integration av den utsatta befolkningen inom agro-livsmedelssystem.

The general purpose of the second phase of the inclusive market project will be to influence the i) intensification of agroecological agriculture, ii) conscious use and consumption of resources and products and iii) social inclusion of the vulnerable population within agri-food systems.

description.narrative:
From June 2023 to May 2024, under the EU-Sweden initiative the project has achieved the following results.
At the impact level, it is important to highlight the contribution to the reduction of greenhouse gases (GHG) of 380 t CO2eq due to the replacement of chemical inputs with biological inputs, exceeding the planned goal by 69%.
Considering the outcomes, three sustainable production models are promoted: i) The organic production model for sesame and organic chia; ii) The transition model towards sustainable agriculture, in extensive crops (grains and legumes) as well as food security and iii) The transition model towards sustainable livestock farming with the validation and incorporation of sustainable practices in grasslands with livestock companies (medium and large) and Mennonite communities in Chiquitanía.
At the same time, the use of bio inputs as a response to the attack of pests, diseases, parasites and the degradation of grasslands is the gateway to the implementation or transition to more sustainable production models. During the reporting period, the project has introduced these sustainable management practices in more than 29,500 hectares of large, medium and small peasant and indigenous producers, exceeding the planned goal by 196%.
In this period, more than 3,600 producers have received assistance and technical innovations in sustainable production models, exceeding the management goal by 23% and more than 550 have accessed markets and/or financial services, achieving 69% of the planned goal. These results make it possible to strengthen the livelihoods of rural and indigenous communities, based on the use and comprehensive management of their natural resources in a context of climate change.
Finally, regarding women economic empowerment, more than 1,400 women have been strengthened in a sustainable production and/or market development approach (41% more than the planned goal) and more than 680 women have accessed technology, markets, inputs and/or financial services (37% more than the planned goal) thus contributing to greater economic empowerment under a sustainable production approach.
It is also important to mention that the project has had results in other territories (Altiplano and Inter-Andean Valleys) during the management from June 2023 to May 2024 within the framework of the contribution of Sida´s resources only. These results contribute to results at the national level, consolidating the actions initiated in the 2022 management (beginning of the phase). Among the main results it can be mentioned:
Development and Access to Product Markets
602 producers (256 women and 346 men) from the Altiplano and Inter-Andean Valleys have accessed markets and technical assistance services (harvest, post-harvest and improved packaging) for products in the fields of valley fruits, vegetables, tubers and others. Articulation with international markets (Trade Promotion): By facilitating compliance with international certifications, adapting products for export markets and participating in fairs, 250 t of quinoa exported with gluten free certification and 720 t of quinoa-based multigrain pasta to the United States and Europe that involved GBA laboratory analysis and packaging changes. In the first case, up to 100 small farmers suppliers from Oruro and Potosí benefited and in the second case the company increased its sales by 20% and the price by 3%, favouring 800 families that were suppliers of raw materials.
Services, Supplies, Technology to face Climate Change
2,788 producers (1,742 men and 1,046 women) in the Altiplano and Inter-Andean Valleys apply practices for sustainable management. 3,321 small farmers/small producers (2,078 men and 1,243 women) from rural and indigenous community organizations have received assistance and technical innovations in sustainable production models.
Education and access to financial services
2,068 producers (1,113 men and 955 women) have accessed financial services (credit and savings) 531 producers (353 men and 178 women) have accessed insurance 5,361 producers (3,114 men and 2,247 women) have accessed financial education
Women Economic Empowerment
1,046 women trained in sustainable production approach in the Altiplano and Inter-Andean Valleys 238 women have accessed resources (technology, financial services, markets, inputs) that contribute to their empowerment and inclusion, violence prevention and attention, care economy, among others.
